name: Hauts-de-France
title: Hauts-de-France —
tagline: Lille, Amiens Cathedral, the Somme and the Côte d'Opale.
summary: Hauts-de-France is France's northernmost region, bordering Belgium and facing the Channel. Its people are known for their warmth, and the old saying goes that the sun in the north is in the hearts of the people.
Lille is its lively capital, Amiens has the largest Gothic cathedral in France by volume, and the battlefields of the First World War, from the Somme to Vimy Ridge, are places of remembrance.

sport.intro: RC Lens and LOSC Lille are the big football names, and cycling's Paris–Roubaix, the 'Hell of the North', is run over cobbles each April.

community.intro: Hauts-de-France has strong links to Belgium, Britain and Canada, and people from the north are warmly proud of their roots.

ancestry: Searching for your family's roots? The French National Archives and the departmental archives hold civil registers, parish records and census returns, and many are searchable online.

fr.tagline: Lille, la cathédrale d'Amiens, la Somme et la Côte d'Opale.
summary: Les Hauts-de-France forment la région la plus au nord de la France, à la frontière de la Belgique et face à la Manche. Ses habitants sont réputés pour leur chaleur : on dit que le soleil du Nord est dans le cœur des gens.

Lille en est la capitale animée, Amiens possède la plus grande cathédrale gothique de France par son volume, et les champs de bataille de la Première Guerre mondiale, de la Somme à la crête de Vimy, sont des lieux de mémoire.
